boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Averasborough record (March 16, 1865) in the Carolinas Campaign [February-March 1865]. Kilpatrick's contact of March 15, which the live description includes, and the skirmishing on March 17 are context outside the frozen one-day record. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads XX Corps and XIV Corps (25,992) against Hardee's Corps (5,400); the live field reads 31,392 (US 25,992; CS 5,400). Slocum says he sent two divisions of each corps on the Averasborough road without wagons, the remaining division of each corps going with the trains, and that the four divisions (Jackson's and Ward's of the Twentieth, Morgan's and Carlin's of the Fourteenth) camped near Taylor's Hole Creek on the 15th, with Hawley's brigade sent forward to support the cavalry. NPS says four divisions of the XX Corps arrived during the night. Hardee gives no strength for his own corps; he reports Wheeler coming to his help late on the 16th and later in his rear with 500 or 600 men.
claims.rationale: The frozen US figure is labelled as two whole corps, while Slocum describes four divisions on this road; NPS's 'four divisions of the XX Corps' differs from Slocum's two of each corps. No date or basis for the frozen CS 5,400 was found in this record's families. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Slocum found the Confederates entrenched about a mile and a half from the fork of the Bentonville road; the roads were almost impassable and it was nearly 10 o'clock before his other troops reached the field; the Confederates were driven about a mile to a third line of works after a brief stand at a second. Hardee wrote on the 17th that the roads were almost impassable. NPS places Hardee across the Raleigh road near Smithville and says the XIV Corps could not deploy before dark because of the swampy ground.
claims.rationale: The roads and swamp predate the action; when the three lines of works were built is not stated. The tag stays unresolved.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. Slocum says the Confederates retreated during the night through Averasborough and that he captured 3 guns, a caisson, several ambulances and 175 prisoners. Hardee reports that the Union troops were repulsed in every attempt to carry his lines or turn his flanks, that two guns were abandoned, and that he retired that night. NPS says the Federals drove Hardee from two lines but were repulsed at a third.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Slocum's three captured guns and Hardee's two abandoned guns differ; both are preserved.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads '1,419 total' with no side split; the live field reads 1,547 (US 682; CS 865). Slocum gives the loss in the two corps as 564 killed and wounded, with a compiler's footnote referring to the revised table, and says 128 Confederate dead were buried on the field. In the No. 3 return the Twentieth Corps total line ends at 485 and the garbled Averasborough recapitulation (Fourteenth Corps, Twentieth Corps, cavalry, total) ends '485 81 682'. Hardee gives his loss as between 400 and 500, including Colonel Rhett missing.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The No. 3 return is a later compilation from nominal lists; its regimental columns are largely garbled in OCR and only the final totals are relied on. The Kinston and Bentonville grand-total lines print killed, wounded and missing figures that sum to their totals; the Averasborough recapitulation is garbled and its final 682 is read by position. A live NPS figure that matches it is not independent corroboration. Slocum's 564 excludes the missing and the cavalry; the return's 682 includes both.

open_questions: Williams's No. 130 and Davis's No. 62 reports, the Jackson, Ward and brigade reports, Kilpatrick's Averasborough passage (in the selected Kilpatrick report, not cited here), Wheeler's synopsis entry for March 16 (not cited here), Taliaferro's No. 290 report, McLaws's account and any Confederate casualty return remain deferred. J. E. Johnston's March 18 dispatch (in his selection, not cited here) gives Hardee's loss on the 16th as 450 and relays prisoners' report of the Union loss as about 5,300; his March 27 field return gives Hardee 5,400 infantry on the morning of March 19, the same figure as the frozen CS 5,400. The coincidence is recorded, not adopted, and Johnston is not one of this record's families.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Blair's, G. P. Harrison's, Kilpatrick's, Wheeler's, J. D. Cox's, Bragg's, Slocum's, Hardee's and J. E. Johnston's reports and dispatches, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVII, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. The No. 3 return of Union casualties is a compiler's table from nominal lists, used as the one targeted follow-up for the casualty gap at Kinston, Averasborough and Bentonville. Cox's history The March to the Sea; Franklin and Nashville (1882) belongs to the same author family as his report. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
